concerns: The audited sources support the food sense in both locales, but they do not establish frequency, regional breadth, or preference over alternatives.
The Malaysian dictionary evidence is community-edited; the cited DBP lead was not audited.
result.rationale: For the intended sense of edible corn, jagung has the same meaning in Indonesian and Malaysian Malay. Dictionary entries support the meaning, and recipes show food use in each locale. Jagung manis is narrower; no supported false-friend contrast appears.
